expect: HTTP 403 Forbidden with no Retry-After and no vendor fingerprint. policy_for_status(403)='disguise' — the crawler should change its network path/UA and retry, not mark the URL dead. evidence: measured 2026-07-26, follow_redirects=False, verify=True, two fetches ~6s apart: 403 / 403, 0 bytes, no Retry-After, no cf-mitigated, no captcha vendor signature. A bare 403 with an empty body, i.e. the case where nothing but the code is available.

expect: HTTP 404 Not Found is terminal: policy 'gone' -> diagnose() returns gone + mark_gone. The URL must never be fetched again. This is the HARD 404, distinct from the soft_404 category where a 200 carries a 'page not found' body.
evidence: measured 2026-07-26, follow_redirects=False, verify=True, two fetches ~6s apart: 404 / 404, 14 bytes, body '{"status":404}', content-type 'application/json; charset=utf-8', server 'cloudflare' (cf-ray a212fa150b853ada-BOM). expect: HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed answering a GET means this URL is not a document at all — an API endpoint that only accepts POST. Unmapped, so policy is 'drop': record and never retry, because retrying the same GET can only produce 405 again.
evidence: measured 2026-07-26, follow_redirects=False, verify=True, two fetches ~6s apart: 405 / 405, 0 bytes, content-type 'text/plain; charset=utf-8'. Cross-checked against the natural form of the same case: GET https://httpbingo.org/post (a POST-only endpoint) also returned 405, 19 bytes.

expect: HTTP 406 Not Acceptable is content negotiation failing — the server has the resource but not in a form the Accept header allows. Policy 'drop'; retrying with the same headers is pointless, and the JSON body naming the acceptable types must not be stored as content.
evidence: measured 2026-07-26, follow_redirects=False, verify=True, two fetches ~6s apart: 406 / 406, 171 bytes, content-type 'application/json; charset=utf-8', body '{{ "message": "Client did not request a supported media type", "accept": ["image/webp","image/svg+xml","image/jpeg","image/png","image/*"] }}'.

expect: HTTP 408 Request Timeout is the one 4xx that is explicitly retryable: policy_for_status(408)='retry_later'. The crawler must requeue rather than drop — this is the row that proves 4xx is not uniformly terminal.
evidence: measured 2026-07-26, follow_redirects=False, verify=True, two fetches ~6s apart: 408 / 408, 0 bytes, content-type 'text/plain; charset=utf-8'. evidence: measured 2026-07-26, follow_redirects=False, verify=True, two fetches ~6s apart: 429 / 429, 0 bytes, content-type 'text/plain; charset=utf-8'.
